methodology.metaTitle: VPN Comparison Methodology — Sources and Criteria
methodology.metaDescription: VPN Advisor's source-based comparison approach: official documentation, independent audits, pricing, privacy, freshness and limitations.
methodology.h1: Our VPN Information and Comparison Methodology
methodology.intro: Provider profiles on this site use the same source framework across five information areas. Ad revenue does not change how evidence is classified — this page explains our sources, uncertainty and the limits of not running provider performance tests.

independence.title: 1. Independence and Revenue Disclosure
independence.intro: To earn your trust we openly disclose our revenue model. Primary revenue comes from Google AdSense ads and, where programs exist, VPN affiliate links. Commission does not affect rankings.
independence.withAffiliateBody: Revenue comes from Google AdSense and some provider affiliate programs. Affiliate commission does not change editorial scores or rankings; providers without affiliate programs (e.g. Mullvad) remain listed.
independence.withoutAffiliateBody: All providers, including Mullvad, are scored against the same criteria. Ad revenue does not influence rankings or scores — this is the most concrete signal of our impartiality.

pledgeItems.0: We do not buy subscriptions to run laboratory or field tests, and we do not accept free or sponsored accounts as a basis for editorial trust claims.
pledgeItems.1: No provider has pre-publication review, edit or veto rights over our content.
pledgeItems.2: Rankings, scores and critical notes are the responsibility of the editorial team; sales and marketing have no input.
pledgeItems.3: A provider's score is calculated independently of ad revenue; a brand running ads does not move it higher in the ranking.

independence.linkText: See the Advertising Disclosure page for full details.

tests.title: 2. Source and information framework
tests.intro: Every provider profile is classified across the same information areas using official documents, independent audits and standards. These are reading and verification criteria, not a testing protocol.

speed.title: a) How to read performance information
speed.summary: We do not publish a fixed editorial speed result; we explain how protocol, route, device, ISP and server load can change outcomes.
speed.tools: Provider documentation, protocol standards and independent tools that readers can run on their own connection.
speed.locationsLabel: Why there is no single result
speed.locations: Routes such as Istanbul, Frankfurt or New York can produce different outcomes because distance and ISP routing differ.

methodSteps.0: Record a VPN-off baseline and then a VPN-on value on the same device and time window.
methodSteps.1: Compare the same or nearby endpoint and, where possible, the same protocol.
methodSteps.2: Repeat measurements and note variation, latency and packet loss instead of relying on one number.
methodSteps.3: Separate busy and quiet hours; do not generalise your result to every reader.
methodSteps.4: Interpret the result as a property of your connection at that time, not as a VPN Advisor test.

speed.metrics: Download, upload, ping, jitter and packet loss; this site does not record provider lab measurements.

security.title: b) Security and leak information
security.summary: We explain provider-documented protections and the limits of one-time diagnostics readers can run on their own device.
security.tools: ipleak.net, dnsleaktest.com (extended test), browserleaks.com (WebRTC + canvas), test-ipv6.com, Wireshark (TCP-level packet inspection).

checks.0: IPv4 leak: whether the real IP is exposed while the VPN is active.
checks.1: IPv6 leak: many home connections have IPv6 enabled; does the provider block it?
checks.2: WebRTC leak: the relevant browser and platform limitations are documented separately.
checks.3: DNS leak: do queries go to the VPN's own resolver or to the ISP? Verified via the extended test across 6 different resolvers.
checks.4: Kill switch: the VPN process is forcefully killed during an active connection (Task Manager / kill -9) and we verify that internet access is actually severed.

security.config: We check whether the provider uses its own DNS, whether the default protocol is modern (WireGuard / OpenVPN UDP), the cipher (AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20) and certificate validation.

streaming.title: c) Streaming test
streaming.summary: How reliable is access to geo-restricted platforms?
streaming.platforms: Netflix (US, UK, JP, TR libraries), Disney+, BBC iPlayer, YouTube TV, Amazon Prime Video, BluTV and Exxen.

methodSteps.0: We log into each platform with our own paid subscription via parallel browser sessions.
methodSteps.1: Provider coverage and regional server claims are checked against current official documentation.
methodSteps.2: For providers that offer Smart DNS, obfuscated or streaming-optimised servers, standard and special servers are reported separately.
methodSteps.3: We also record video quality (480p / 1080p / 4K) and buffer time during the test.

streaming.result: Success rate per platform (%) — 9/9 working servers means 100%, none working means 0%.

privacy.title: d) Privacy and no-logs verification
privacy.summary: Evidence-based verification that goes beyond marketing claims.
privacy.audits: No-logs and application-security reports published by PwC, Deloitte, KPMG, Cure53, Securitum and Assured AB are read in their original form. The scope (servers, code or configuration), cadence and limitations of each report feed into the score.
privacy.jurisdiction: We review which 5/9/14-Eyes alliance the provider's home office belongs to, data-retention laws and history of legal compulsion. Jurisdictions like Panama, Switzerland and BVI are advantageous; the US and UK are disadvantageous.
privacy.policy: The privacy policy and terms are read end to end. Existence of a transparency report and a warrant canary is checked.
privacy.infra: Claims of RAM-only servers (no disks, everything wiped on reboot) are validated against provider documentation and independent reports.

usability.title: e) Usability, support and quality
usability.summary: The details that make daily use pleasant or painful.
usability.apps: Windows, macOS, iOS, Android and Linux apps are installed on real devices; install time, first connect time and UI ergonomics are documented.
usability.daily: Each VPN is used daily for at least 14 days: browsing, email, video calls, gaming and file transfer. Unstable connections, unexpected drops and battery drain are reported.
usability.support: We contact live chat at 3 different times (morning, afternoon, night). Response time, resolution quality and whether the agent actually has technical knowledge are evaluated.
usability.refund: Does the money-back guarantee really work? At the end of the test cycle we cancel the subscription and request a refund; we report whether the process is friction-free, how many days it takes and how much is actually refunded.

scoring.title: 3. Scoring System
scoring.intro: The results of the five test categories are mapped onto six scoring dimensions. Each dimension is rated 1–10 and contributes to the final score with the weights below.

security.name: Security
security.description: Leak-test results, kill-switch reliability, encryption standard, audit coverage.

privacy.name: Privacy
privacy.description: Jurisdiction, no-logs audits, RAM-only infrastructure, transparency report.

speed.name: Speed
speed.description: Percentage drop versus baseline; weighted average across three regions.

streaming.name: Streaming
streaming.description: Weighted average of per-platform success rates.

usability.name: Usability
usability.description: App quality, support response time, ease of first-time setup.

pricing.name: Pricing
pricing.description: Renewal-price transparency, true monthly cost, refund policy terms.

scoring.formula: Final score = Σ(dimension score × weight). Published as a decimal between 0.0 and 10.0.

freshness.title: 4. Freshness Policy
freshness.intro: The VPN market changes quickly. An independent audit may be strong evidence today and require a fresh scope check later. We therefore show source and pricing check dates clearly.

items.0: Each profile's sources and pricing are rechecked when new documents or material changes appear.
items.1: Each review page shows the relevant source and pricing-check date clearly.
items.2: If a breach, ownership change, new audit or critical feature appears, the relevant content is reassessed.
items.3: Pricing is tracked via a separate 'pricingVerifiedAt' field; we adapt to market price changes within 30 days.

transparency.title: 5. Transparency and Limitations

envItems.0: We do not claim provider performance from a fixed device, ISP or laboratory location.
envItems.1: Official technical documents, privacy policies, terms and pricing pages are primary sources.
envItems.2: Independent audits are read with their scope, date and limitations.
envItems.3: Reader tools provide one-time diagnostics; they do not create a provider score or guarantee.

limitsItems.0: Performance depends on ISP, route, server load and device; we do not publish fixed laboratory results.
limitsItems.1: Streaming success rates change over time — platforms continuously update their VPN detection.
limitsItems.2: We do not run provider field or laboratory tests; reader tools show signals from the current connection only.
limitsItems.3: We state explicitly that no independent certification body audits us; publishing our methodology openly is our strongest quality safeguard.
limitsItems.4: Users should make the final call based on their own priorities (privacy vs speed vs streaming).

transparency.contactBody: If you have a question or suggestion about the methodology, reach out via the contact page. If you find a serious error we verify it, update the affected page and publish a change note.

editorial.title: Editorial independence
editorial.body: We disclose our revenue model transparently (see <link>Advertising Disclosure</link>). The site's revenue comes from Google AdSense ads; we earn no commission from any VPN provider, which is the most direct signal of our impartiality.

privacy.title: Privacy policy and jurisdiction
privacy.body: We evaluate the provider's logging policy, the country its headquarters is in (5/9/14 Eyes alliances, data retention laws) and how it responds to legal requests.

audits.title: Independent audits
audits.body: The presence, frequency and scope of third-party audit reports (Deloitte, KPMG, Cure53, Securitum, Assured AB) drive the weight of this criterion.

speed.title: Speed
speed.body: We assess performance claims through official technical documentation, protocol design and clearly stated limitations.

streaming.title: Streaming compatibility
streaming.body: Access tests on platforms like Netflix US/UK/TR, Disney+, BBC iPlayer, BluTV and Exxen using different servers.

pricing.title: Pricing transparency
pricing.body: The gap between the first-purchase price and the renewal price, hidden fees and the real money-back policy are all reviewed.

usability.title: Ease of use
usability.body: App interface, initial setup time, server-picker ergonomics and customer-support accessibility are all assessed.

calculator.intro: Most VPNs are cheap up front and expensive on renewal. Here you see the true 1/2/3-year total cost — compare fairly on "effective monthly" price.

tool.explanation: How it's calculated: discounted first-term price, then monthly-plan price on renewal. Most providers use a "renewal trap" — cheap up front, 2–3× more after. Disabling auto-renew and re-buying on discount saves money.

howSection.calcBody: For each VPN we take the "best value" plan (typically 2–3 years) as the reference. During the plan term the discounted price applies; after it expires we assume renewal at the monthly-plan rate. This is the source of most Trustpilot complaints — users see "$30 the first year, $120 the second year."
howSection.trapTitle: How to dodge the renewal trap
howSection.trap1Body: — log in to your VPN account and turn off auto-renew in billing settings.
howSection.trap2Body: buy a fresh discounted plan from the same provider or a different one.
howSection.trap3Body: — flat €5/month, no discount/renewal trap. Better for consistency than for squeezing out savings.
howSection.term1Body: The right balance for most users — meaningful discount, manageable commitment.
howSection.term2Body: Lowest effective monthly, but a 3-year commitment to one provider. The VPN market moves fast — even cheap is risky.
howSection.term3Body: Flexibility but 2–3× more expensive. Only for short-term needs.

explainer.title: What is this?
explainer.body: {site} is not a company or institution; it has no registered legal entity. It is a public version of the notes that built up while we were comparing VPN providers for our own use. Google AdSense ad revenue covers infrastructure costs; it does not influence the recommendations. See <disclosure>Advertising disclosure</disclosure> and <legal>Legal notice</legal> for details.

approach.body: We try to make it easier to find clear, independent, source-based information when choosing a VPN. Our assessments come from independent audit reports, public sources and official documentation — not marketing copy. No recommendation is a hard guarantee; the final decision is always yours.

transparent.title: Transparent methodology
transparent.body: Every VPN is scored against the same six criteria. The criteria and their weights are public.

independence.title: Editorial independence
independence.body: Ad revenue does not influence the ranking or the assessment. We list all providers against the same criteria.

evidence.title: Evidence first
evidence.body: Saying "good VPN" isn't enough — independent audits, court rulings or audit reports are required.

howWeTest.body: Every provider profile is organised around the same six information areas: privacy policy and jurisdiction, independent audits, protocols and network details, device support, pricing transparency and use-case context. We do not run provider field or laboratory tests. See our <methodology>methodology page</methodology> for the details.

revenue.body1: We finance this site through Google AdSense ad revenue. Pages show ads served by Google; links to VPN providers are plain, non-commercial links and we earn no commission from them. We explain this in detail on the <disclosure>Advertising disclosure</disclosure> page.
revenue.body2: Important: Ad revenue does not influence the ranking. We rank all providers (including e.g. Mullvad) against the same criteria; a brand running ads does not get placed at the top.

authors.body: {site} started as a personal project. Content is produced through volunteer contributions; there is no professional newsroom or editorial staff. The primary sources are providers' own audit reports, publicly available court documents, open-source repositories and our own observations. If you find anything wrong or missing, please let us know — we take corrections seriously.

why.body: Commercial VPN reviews are mostly sales-driven; "best" claims get repeated without sources. {site} is a reference project that started as a hobby and grew more systematic over time, written into that gap. The goal is not to give a single "correct answer" — it's to provide structured information so the reader can make their own call.

items.q: What can websites see about me?
items.a: A website can see your public IP address and request metadata, plus browser-provided signals such as browser family, operating system, screen size, language, timezone and whether cookies are enabled.

items.q: Can a website see my MAC address?
items.a: No. Normal websites cannot read your local MAC address through standard browser APIs.

items.q: Does this tool prove that I am anonymous?
items.a: No. This tool is a transparency snapshot, not an anonymity guarantee. Accounts, cookies, device settings and other signals can still identify or link activity.

vpnTest.checking: Checking your public IP and connection details...
vpnTest.errorTitle: The check could not be completed
vpnTest.errorBody: The diagnostic service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
vpnTest.rateLimitedBody: Too many checks were requested from this connection. Please wait a minute and try again.
vpnTest.degradedNote: The external lookup is unavailable, so we are showing only the IP and location details available from request headers.
vpnTest.privacyNote: This check sends your public IP to ipapi.is for network classification. VPN Advisor does not intentionally store the result.
vpnTest.detectionDetected: Datacenter, proxy or VPN signals detected
vpnTest.detectionClear: No datacenter, proxy or VPN signals detected
vpnTest.detectionCaveat: VPN, proxy and datacenter detection is heuristic. Some residential VPNs may look clean, and some business or cloud networks may be flagged.
vpnTest.explainBody: This tool checks the public IP address visible to websites, approximate location, provider details and optional risk signals. It does not inspect your traffic, install anything or expose API keys in the browser.

emailSecurity.metaTitle: Email Security Check - Free Breach, SPF, DMARC and MX Test
emailSecurity.metaDescription: Check an email address for domain security signals: MX, SPF, DMARC, disposable address risk and optional Have I Been Pwned breach matches. Free and privacy-conscious.
emailSecurity.title: Email Security Check
emailSecurity.subtitle: Check whether an email address sits on a properly protected domain and, when configured, whether Have I Been Pwned has breach signals for it.
emailSecurity.invalidEmail: Enter a valid email address and try again.
emailSecurity.errorTitle: The email check could not be completed
emailSecurity.errorBody: The security check is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
emailSecurity.rateLimitedBody: Too many checks were requested from this connection. Please wait a minute and try again.
emailSecurity.privacyDetail: Your full email address is sent to VPN Advisor's server for this check. The domain is queried for live MX, SPF and DMARC records, and the address is sent server-to-server to Have I Been Pwned when configured, otherwise XposedOrNot. VPN Advisor does not intentionally retain the address or result; no API keys are sent to the browser.
emailSecurity.noFindings: No urgent issues were found. Keep 2FA enabled and avoid reusing passwords.

mx.title: MX records
mx.pass: This domain can receive email through configured mail servers.
mx.fail: No MX records were found. The address may not be able to receive email.

spf.title: SPF
spf.pass: SPF is present and uses an enforcement mechanism.
spf.warning: SPF exists, but the policy is weak or incomplete.
spf.fail: No SPF record was found. Spoofed email is easier from this domain.

dmarc.title: DMARC
dmarc.pass: DMARC is configured with quarantine or reject policy.
dmarc.warning: DMARC is present but only monitors mail with p=none.
dmarc.fail: No DMARC policy was found. Phishing protection is weaker.

breach.clear: No known breach was found for this address in the breach database.
breach.found: This address appears in one or more known breaches.
breach.unavailable: The breach database is temporarily unavailable. MX, SPF and DMARC results were fetched via live DNS lookups.

findings.breach_found: Change the password for this email and every reused password. Turn on 2FA for important accounts.
findings.hibp_not_configured: Breach database check is unavailable right now; MX, SPF and DMARC results are still live DNS lookups.
findings.hibp_unavailable: The breach database could not be reached. Re-run the check later.
findings.no_mx: The domain has no MX records. Check the address or use a different email.
findings.no_spf: Ask the domain owner to add SPF so fake senders are harder to spoof.
findings.weak_spf: Tighten the SPF policy and avoid permissive mechanisms such as +all.
findings.no_dmarc: Add DMARC with at least monitoring, then move toward quarantine or reject.
findings.dmarc_monitor_only: DMARC is monitoring only. Move toward quarantine or reject after reviewing reports.
findings.disposable_email: Disposable email domains are risky for important accounts. Use a durable mailbox.
findings.role_account: Role accounts are often shared. Use unique users, strong passwords and 2FA.

emailSecurity.explainTitle: What this email security check does
emailSecurity.explainBody: The tool validates the email format, checks the domain's MX, SPF and DMARC records via live DNS queries, flags common disposable or shared role addresses and searches known breach databases (Have I Been Pwned when configured, otherwise XposedOrNot). Results are not simulated.
emailSecurity.scoreCaveat: This is a triage score for visible signals, not a certification that the account or mailbox is secure.

dns.metaDescription: Inspect DNS resolver signals from your current browser connection. This diagnostic does not prove system-wide VPN behavior.
dns.title: DNS Resolver Check
dns.subtitle: Inspect which resolver signals this browser session exposes while your VPN is on. The result is not a system-wide verdict.
dns.experimentalTitle: Experimental tool — does not test your system DNS
dns.experimentalBody: This browser check queries Cloudflare DoH (1.1.1.1); it does not measure your operating system's complete DNS path. Compare with a server-side tool and your provider documentation.
dns.noLeakBody: One resolver signal appeared in this browser check. Verify its ownership and whether other applications use the same path.
dns.leakBody: Multiple resolver signals appeared. This is not proof that every DNS query leaves through the ISP; compare with another server-side check.
dns.explainTitle: What is a DNS leak, why is it dangerous?
dns.explainBody: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses. Even when you use a VPN, misconfiguration can route DNS queries to your ISP, exposing your browsing history.

webrtc.metaTitle: WebRTC Signal Check - Public IP Visibility
webrtc.metaDescription: Inspect whether this browser session exposes a public IP through WebRTC while a VPN is on. Treat the result as a signal.
webrtc.title: WebRTC Signal Check
webrtc.subtitle: WebRTC supports browser calls and may expose network signals depending on browser permissions and configuration. This check is not a universal leak verdict.
webrtc.noLeak: No public IP observed in this check
webrtc.noLeakBody: No public IP signal appeared through WebRTC in this check. This does not guarantee every network or browser context.
webrtc.leakBody: WebRTC returned a public IP signal. Review browser permissions and VPN settings, then compare on another network.
webrtc.fixChrome: Chrome: install the WebRTC Network Limiter extension.
webrtc.fixFirefox: Firefox: open about:config and set media.peerconnection.enabled to false.
webrtc.fixBrave: Brave: Settings > Privacy > WebRTC IP handling policy = Default Public Interface Only.

speed.metaTitle: VPN Speed Comparison - Free Connection Diagnostic 2026
speed.metaDescription: Compare download and latency signals with your VPN on and off using Cloudflare infrastructure. Results describe your connection, not a provider average.
speed.title: VPN Speed Comparison
speed.subtitle: Run this check with your VPN on and off under the same conditions, then compare the signals from your current connection.
speed.error: The speed test could not complete. Check your connection and try again — some corporate networks or ad blockers may block the Cloudflare test server.
speed.embedNote: For a more in-depth test use Cloudflare's official tool.
speed.explainTitle: How should you interpret VPN speed changes?
speed.explainBody: A VPN can add encryption and a new route. The change depends on device, Wi-Fi, ISP, route, server load and protocol; there is no universal percentage. Repeat comparable checks before drawing a conclusion.
speed.comparisonHint: Run once, save that result as a baseline (for example with VPN off), then run again under comparable conditions.
